Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Daniel said by phone that he had written her name beside that time in his diary, although the room is only held after the deposit has gone through. So for now the teacher time seems fairly settled, while the room booking still depends on payment being recorded.

Mara has played violin for around six years, with a long break of about four years in the middle. She started again last autumn and has been practising on most weeks, usually three times a week, though sometimes work makes it only once. She has a full-size instrument and a shoulder rest, and she will bring both. The violin was checked by a repair shop in January, but the E string has started to sound a little thin when she plays near the bridge. She is not sure whether that is her bowing or the string, so she would like Daniel to listen before they decide there is a repair needed. She has a spare E string at home but does not plan to change it before the lesson.

The reason for booking is that she wants to get more secure with shifting and intonation, and she would also like to prepare a short piece for a neighborhood spring gathering in May. She has not chosen the piece yet. Her previous teacher suggested the first movement of Vivaldi's Concerto in A minor, but Mara thinks that may be slightly ambitious right now. She is open to working on it if Daniel feels it is manageable, but she does not want the whole lesson to turn into a decision about repertoire. She would prefer a few minutes on posture and bow hold first, because those things have become less reliable since she returned to playing.

Daniel described the first meeting this way: “I can keep the first ten minutes for tuning, but I can't promise that we'll get through every piece.” Mara said that sounded reasonable, and she is not expecting to finish a piece in one lesson. She asked whether she should send a recording beforehand. Daniel said it was optional, and that a phone recording was enough if she wanted to share one. Mara has not sent anything yet. She might record the opening of the Vivaldi later in the week, but she wants to check the score and make sure she is playing from the same edition first. The edition she owns is the Schirmer one, marked with pencil from her earlier lessons.

Booking and arrival details: the requested lesson is 45 minutes, on Thursday, April 17, starting at 6:15 p.m. The address on the booking page is 28 Larch Street, with the entrance through the glass door beside the bakery. Daniel said the room is on the second floor and there is no lift. Mara can manage the stairs, but she will carry the violin in its case and does not want to bring a music stand. The studio has a stand in each room. She asked whether she should arrive early to tune, and Daniel suggested arriving five minutes beforehand rather than waiting in the corridor for a long time.

2. What Mara will bring: her violin, bow, shoulder rest, and the Schirmer score if she decides to use it. She will also bring a small notebook because she often forgets instructions once she gets home. She does not need to bring rosin unless Daniel asks, since the bow was rosined recently. She asked if there is a piano in the room; Daniel said there is an electric keyboard, which he can use for reference pitches, but it is not available for students to practise on before the lesson. There is a water fountain downstairs. Mara usually brings a bottle anyway, particularly after coming straight from work.

Daniel asked her to tell him if she has a specific technique concern that should take priority. She said shifting is the main concern, but intonation is closely connected to it for her, and she does not want a rigid list of exercises with no explanation. She is comfortable with direct correction, though she sometimes needs an example played slowly before she can understand what has changed. She has no injury, but her left shoulder can feel slightly tense after a longer practice session. She thinks this is more likely when she is tired than when she plays a particular passage. She does not want to treat that as a medical issue; she is mentioning it so they can pay attention to posture and take a short pause if needed.

The payment is £32 for the 45-minute lesson. Daniel sent a payment link after the call, and Mara opened it but has not paid yet because she wants to confirm the date in the booking page first. The page showed a £10 deposit, with the remaining £22 due at the lesson. Daniel said the deposit is credited toward the fee and is not an additional charge. The payment link expires after 24 hours. If the deposit is not recorded before it expires, the slot is released and Mara will need to contact him again; he has not said that he can hold it without payment. She asked whether cash would be accepted for the balance, and he said cash or bank transfer was fine.

For travel, Mara expects to take the 5:42 bus from the office area and walk from the Larch Street stop. The route normally takes about twelve minutes, though traffic occasionally makes the bus late. Daniel told her, “If you're more than ten minutes behind, send me a text so I know whether to wait; the lesson still has to finish at 7:00.” Mara understood that the end time would not move if she arrived late. She has Daniel's mobile number from the booking page and will use text rather than calling while she is on the bus. If the bus is delayed but she can still arrive within ten minutes, she has not been told that she needs to send an update.

The cancellation terms on the booking page say that a change or cancellation made at least 24 hours before the lesson can be moved once without losing the deposit. A later cancellation means the deposit is kept, except where Daniel agrees otherwise. Mara has not asked to change the date; she is including the terms here because her daughter has an occasional school event on Thursdays and the May dates are not known yet. The booking page does not say whether a replacement date has to be within the same week. Daniel has not answered that question, and Mara has not treated the deposit as paid.
